1.why: Complete 2x2 grid of {1,6} x {+,-}: every option is the mirror of another, so no value is distinguished.

2.why: 400 is the derivational hub - 1200 = 3x400, 120 = 0.3x400, 403 = 400+3 - and I bet the generator, not the derived values, is the key.

3.why: All four crossings of x in {5,-1} with y in {-1,-9} are present, a closed coordinate grid that narrows nothing.

4.why: -0.5 and 2 are negative reciprocals so the key is probably that pair, but choosing inside it is a coin flip; I take the integer over the lone decimal.

5.why: Non-numeric set, but the shape is a full sign grid (x+-3 over x+-2) - all four are equally legal rational expressions, so the form narrows nothing.

6.why: A +-32 pair plus two small consecutive integers; nothing is lone in form or value.

7.why: 25 is a lone perfect square and 7 carries a sign twin, two weak signals pointing opposite ways, so this is a coin flip.

8.why: Complete 2x2 grid {3,4} x {+,-} with no odd form, no outlier, no derivable member.

9.why: Two perfect squares (9, 25) against two small negatives (-1, -2) - a balanced 2-and-2 split with no lone member.

10.why: Non-numeric: the set DOES narrow by shape - 8000(1.06/12)^m decays and 8000(1.06)^(12m) explodes, leaving only the two plausible growth forms - but between (1.06)^(m/12) and (1+0.06/12)^m nothing in the values decides, so this is 50/50 after a real 4-to-2 leak.

11.why: 18 is the hub: 324 = 18^2, -18 is its negation, 81 = (18/2)^2; the three others are all manufactured from it.

12.why: 10 loosely hubs the set (-10 negation, 5 = 10/2) but -2 does not fit the family cleanly enough to call it.

13.why: Non-numeric: a full 2x2 of {between, outside} x {(-2,8), (-8,2)} - the interval shapes are perfectly symmetric and narrow nothing.

14.why: 20, 44, 72, 120 form no arithmetic or geometric run and no member is a simple combination of two others.

15.why: 27 is the hub of a 3-9-27 geometric family plus its own negation, with 5 the outlier; I bet the generator over the derived 9 and the sign trap.

16.why: -1/3 is the lone fraction and 0 the lone special value, which by my directional bet makes both baits, leaving the consecutive pair 12/13 undecided between them.

17.why: 8 is the hub - 64 = 8^2, 4 = 8/2 - while 49 is the lone odd, non-power-of-2 outlier.

18.why: 9 is the middle of the 3-9-81 geometric run with 36 the outlier, and it also hubs the set (36 = 4x9); the measured middle-of-run channel and the hub rule agree here.

19.why: 3 is the hub: 1/3 is its reciprocal, 12 = 4x3 and 24 = 8x3, so every other option is manufactured from it.

20.why: Non-numeric: all four crossings of x in {3,12} with y in {5,10} are present, so the coordinate shape narrows nothing.

21.why: 2.5 is the lone decimal and by my bet a bait, but the remaining 6, 9, 21 form no run and nothing separates them.

22.why: 79 is a lone large outlier but 3, 7, 16 are mutually unrelated, so removing it leaves a three-way coin flip.

23.why: 48.8 + 51.2 = 100 is a complementary percentage pair that must contain the key, and 51.2 = 0.8 x 64 is computed from another option in the set while 48.8 is only its complement - the took-the-complement error.

24.why: 0 is the lone special value and therefore a bait, but 5, 6, 9 are undistinguished among themselves.
